exposure: maternal BMI group (low BMI < 22.6 kg/m2, middle-range BMI 22.7-28.0 kg/m2, high BMI > 28.0 kg/m2)
outcome: villous changes related to maternal malperfusion
cohort: The study included 295 patients diagnosed with preeclampsia and a singleton pregnancy, delivered between 2008 and 2021 at a single tertiary medical center.
finding: Neonatal birth weight and placental weight were significantly decreased in the low maternal BMI group, while both extremes of BMI (low and high) were associated with higher rates of placental maternal vascular malperfusion.
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured as an outcome, with significant decreases observed in the low maternal BMI group, but no specific weight range for inclusion of all participants was mentioned.
